subject: biology
title: Balanced diet and nutrients
key_idea: A balanced diet contains all the nutrient groups in the right proportions, with the right amount of energy for the person's lifestyle. Each nutrient has its own sources and its own job. Too little vitamin C causes scurvy. Too little vitamin D or calcium causes rickets.

blocks.text: A diet is the food a person usually eats. This section covers what makes it balanced.

items.meaning: A diet that contains all the nutrients, in the correct proportions, and gives the right amount of energy for the person's activity and lifestyle.

items: It must include carbohydrate, fat, protein, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
The proportions matter: too much or too little of one nutrient is not balanced.
Energy needs differ between people, so a balanced diet differs too.
A balanced diet has all the nutrient groups.
They must be in the correct proportions and give the right amount of energy.

blocks.text: Each nutrient group has main food sources and a main job in the body. The table gives both.

rows: Butter, cooking oil, nuts, oily fish
Source and store of energy. Insulation under the skin
Growth and repair of cells and tissues
Keeps skin and the lining of blood vessels healthy. Wounds heal
Oily fish, eggs, margarine. Also made in the skin in sunlight
Helps the body absorb calcium for bones and teeth
Milk, cheese, fish eaten with the bones
Makes bones and teeth hard. Also needed for blood clotting
Makes haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen
Gives bulk so the muscles of the gut can push food along, which prevents constipation
A solvent. Used in transport and in chemical reactions. Helps control temperature

diagram.alt: Nine nutrients. Tap each one to see its main sources and what it does in the body.
diagram.prompt: Tap a nutrient to see where it comes from and why the body needs it.

parts.name: Carbohydrate
parts.detail: From bread, rice, pasta and potatoes. It is the main source of energy.

parts.name: Fats and oils
parts.detail: From butter, oils and nuts. A store of energy, and insulation under the skin.

parts.name: Protein
parts.detail: From meat, fish, eggs and beans. Needed for growth and repair of tissues.

parts.name: Vitamin C
parts.detail: From citrus fruits and fresh vegetables. Keeps skin healthy. Lack of it causes scurvy.

parts.name: Vitamin D
parts.detail: From oily fish and eggs, and made in the skin in sunlight. Helps absorb calcium. Lack of it causes rickets.

parts.name: Calcium
parts.detail: From milk and cheese. Builds strong bones and teeth.

parts.name: Iron
parts.detail: From red meat and spinach. Needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells.

parts.name: Fibre
parts.detail: From wholemeal bread, fruit and vegetables. Gives bulk so food is moved along the gut.

parts.name: Water
parts.detail: From drinks and food. A solvent, and needed for transport and chemical reactions.

items: Carbohydrate and fat give energy. Protein is for growth and repair.
Calcium and vitamin D make bones and teeth. Iron makes haemoglobin.
Fibre moves food along the gut. Water is a solvent.

blocks.text: A deficiency disease happens when the diet lacks a nutrient for a long time. Two are worth knowing.

rows: Bleeding gums. Wounds heal slowly. Weak blood vessels
Not enough vitamin D or calcium
Soft, weak bones that bend in children

items: Without vitamin D the body cannot absorb enough calcium, so bones stay soft.
Milk with added vitamin D gives children both vitamin D and calcium.
Lack of iron causes anaemia, because less haemoglobin is made.
Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
Rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin D or calcium.

checks.q: Describe what is meant by a balanced diet.
checks.a: A diet with all the nutrients, in the correct proportions, giving the right amount of energy for the person's activity.

checks.q: Name the nutrient whose lack causes scurvy and give one food that contains it.
checks.a: Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits or fresh vegetables.

checks.q: Explain why children are advised to eat foods that contain calcium and vitamin D.
checks.a: Calcium makes bones and teeth hard. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. Together they prevent rickets.

worked_example.question: As part of a balanced diet, some governments recommend that children drink milk that has vitamin D added to it. Suggest the dietary reasons for this advice.
answer_points: Calcium and vitamin D are needed for healthy, strong bones and teeth.
Calcium and vitamin D prevent rickets, or any of its symptoms.
Vitamin D stimulates absorption of calcium.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. Link each nutrient to what it does.

worked_example.question: A balanced diet should include the correct proportions of each component. Two of these components are vitamins and minerals. Describe the functions of the other components of a balanced diet.
answer_points: Carbohydrate is for energy, through respiration.
Lipid (fat) is for energy, storage, insulation or protecting organs.
Protein is for growth and repair, or to make enzymes, hormones and antibodies.
Water is a solvent and is used for transport and chemical reactions.
Fibre moves food along the gut (peristalsis) and prevents constipation.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each component with a correct function. Name the component and its job.

blocks.text: This course adds vitamin A, and asks how energy needs change.

items: **Vitamin A** is needed for good vision. It comes from liver, carrots and dairy foods.
Energy requirements are higher with more activity, such as sport or a physical job.
Older adults need less energy than teenagers and young adults because they are usually less active.
Teenagers need more energy than adults because they are growing.
A pregnant woman needs more energy, protein and minerals such as calcium and iron for the growing foetus.
A person who eats less energy than they need uses stored fat, so body mass falls.
